The loop-jump and playground speed tests do their work once, not per fill or per 60 fps frame (rich-animation-42lg.xkk) (#543)

* The loop-jump and playground speed tests do their work once, not per fill or per 60 fps frame (rich-animation-42lg.xkk)

The loop-jump check computed each frame's field once per fill, touched every
cell anew though a frame holds few distinct shares, and converted each color
to OKLCH at both its steps; it now does each once, the same values compared.
The playground's speed test reads only the readout, so it plays at 1 fps, as
the seek test beside it already does. Alone: 5.4/7.1/14.4s -> 0.3/2.1/3.6s
and 6.8s -> 0.3s; full suite at load ~28: worst 9.0s against the 30s timeout.

* Review: the playground speed test checks it reached 1 fps; the loop-jump comment says it measures the raw field, not the snapped one (rich-animation-42lg.xkk)

* Review: one helper clicks the playground to 1 fps and checks it landed; the loop-jump comment says snapped loops exceed the bar (rich-animation-42lg.xkk)
Review: a scrub drag ends on a move with no button, the track keeps a cell, a marquee's refusal names marquee, hostDepth throws on a depth no step reproduces (rich-animation-42lg.xoj)
Review: the marquee crosses the slot it draws, cyclic copies and refuses a fractional turn, the scrub seeks on the left button, the depth reads writesToTerminal (rich-animation-42lg.xoj)
The animation playground is a readable example: kinds a few to a file, a draggable scrub bar, four colour depths (rich-animation-42lg.xoj)
cyclic and marquee: a rotation through a list, and content of any width crossing a slot a cell a step (rich-animation-42lg.xoj)
